picks.title: Brain researchers afflict LLMs with 'injuries' similar to those of stroke victims to unpack AI language mechanisms
picks.rationale: Fresh peer-reviewed result (Patterns): lesioned LLMs reproduce human aphasia error patterns, so clinical neuroscience tests become a probe for AI language mechanisms.
picks.excerpt: University of South Carolina aphasia researchers (Julius Fridriksson) lesioned layers of large language models and gave them the same tests used on post-stroke patients (Patterns). The damaged models produced error patterns resembling human aphasia, offering a clinical-neuroscience framework for probing LLMs.

picks.title: Ancient Maya site uncovered with 'vibe archaeology' ignites firestorm over AI in science
picks.rationale: Corrects a viral claim (AI agents did not find the Maya site) and reports the live dispute over how AI use should be credited in research; a new humanities angle not covered before.
picks.excerpt: Contrary to viral claims, AI agents did not discover an ancient Maya site, but the episode sparked a clash among archaeologists over how AI tools should be used and credited in science.

picks.title: When AI misidentifies wildlife: New study maps where species identification fails
picks.rationale: Hard numbers on a frontier model's limits for field biology: GPT-5.2 got 9.5% species-level accuracy on 10,000 iNaturalist photos, a concrete caution for anyone using LLMs to identify species.
picks.excerpt: A Biodiversity Data Journal study tested OpenAI's GPT-5.2 on 10,000 iNaturalist photos of Colombian vertebrates and found only 9.5% species-level accuracy, under 5% for amphibians, birds and fishes, even when told the location.

picks.title: Theorizer comes to Asta
picks.rationale: Primary-source tool release usable now: Ai2's Asta agent gains Theorizer, which pulls findings from papers and synthesizes candidate theories with every claim linked to its supporting studies.
picks.excerpt: Ai2 added Theorizer to its Asta science agent: it extracts findings from papers into templates and synthesizes candidate theories, each claim linked to supporting studies. No benchmark numbers reported.

picks.title: An AI-powered 'supertelescope' could revolutionize astronomy—provided someone builds it
picks.rationale: Adds astronomy to the mix: a proposal to fuse Rubin, Euclid and Roman pixels with AI into a sharper virtual fourth observatory for dark-matter and dark-energy work.
picks.excerpt: Astronomers led by Gioia Rau propose using AI to fuse overlapping pixels from Rubin, Euclid and Roman into a virtual fourth observatory with sharper images for dark-matter and dark-energy studies, petabytes at a time.
